chunks: A man trims some of his hair with his teeth; should he wipe it with water before he performs salat (prayer)? He said: “There is no harm; that only applies in the case of iron.”
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What the first report contains, that he should wipe the place with water, is to be understood as recommendation rather than obligation. That is indicated by the following.
(1012) 4. What Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Aʿraj, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: I clip my nails, trim my moustache, and shave my head—must I perform ghusl (ritual bath)? He said: “No, there is no ghusl upon you.”
I said: Then should I perform wudu (ablution)? He said: “No, there is no wudu upon you.”
I said: Then should I wipe water over my nails? He said: “No; it is pure, and there is no wiping required of you.”

key_terms.بِالْمَاءِ: with water, as an act of wiping or cleansing

ai.seo_question: Does clipping nails, trimming hair, or shaving the head require ghusl, wudu, or washing before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report addresses rulings related to ritual purity after trimming hair, clipping nails, trimming the moustache, and shaving the head. It states that none of these acts require ghusl, wudu, or wiping with water, and Shaykh al-Ṭūsī clarifies that any earlier instruction to wipe with water is to be understood as recommended, not obligatory.
